text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) usually causes no symptoms. It is often called the "silent killer" because people can have it for years without knowing.
Typical Symptoms (Only During Spikes or Severe Levels)
When blood pressure becomes extremely high or rises very quickly, you might notice:

list.snippet: Headaches (especially dull, persistent, early-morning headaches at the back of the head)
Shortness of breath during light activity or rest
Heart palpitations or a pounding sensation in your chest, neck, or ears
Tinnitus (ringing or buzzing in the ears)

text_blocks.snippet: According to the Cleveland Clinic, the only reliable way to know your status is by checking your numbers regularly with a blood pressure cuff.
A blood pressure reading above 180/120 mm Hg is dangerously high. If your reading is this high and you experience any of the following signs, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room immediately:

list.snippet: Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
Numbness or weakness in the face, arm, or leg (signs of a stroke)
